## MANUAL AC VERIFICATION — all 14 criteria checked against `gerrit/main`, one by one

Operator-directed (2026-08-05): the completion gate **provably cannot run** on this epic
([rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]), so the operator directed a manual verification of every acceptance
criterion followed by a `--force-close`. This comment is the evidence that substitutes for the
verifier's verdict. Every claim below was checked against the merged tree, not against the checkbox.

| # | criterion | verification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | every child closed + `Verified +1` | **59/59 descendants closed, 0 uncertified** — every one carries a `completion-verifier` signature. Gerrit half: each child's change is MERGED, and merge requires `Verified +1` (only the CI bot casts it; self-approval is impossible) |
| 2 | contract fixture includes `jira-datacenter` | `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py:23` — `@pytest.fixture(params=["fake", "jira", "jira-datacenter"])`, importing `JiraDataCenterBackend` at `:18` |
| 3 | ADR records the sub-seam | `docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md` |
| 4 | [operator-attested] bidirectional reconcile | attested on harness run **30933704255** with both directional cells named and passing; re-confirmed on 30944241768. Marked `[operator-attested]` = not code-verifiable |
| 5 | one implementation per shared unit | `sanitize_label` and `classify_probe_response` each have exactly ONE implementation in `adapters/jira_family/`; the per-backend definitions are **delegating wrappers** — verified by reading them (`jira/probe.py:102` "delegates to the shared `jira_family` classifier"; `jira_datacenter/backend.py:181` `return _shared_sanitize_label(label)`) |
| 6 | Cloud oracles committed BEFORE the extraction | `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_characterization.py` added **2026-07-22 17:34**; the extraction `0c8d392608` "62d9: extract the Jira-family shared layer" landed **2026-07-29 10:18** — oracle precedes extraction by a week. These oracles later PROVED their worth: tightening the shared label constant turned four of them red and blocked a Cloud regression |
| 7 | DC exercised by the backend-agnostic suite | same fixture as (2) — not adapter-local tests |
| 8 | clean core pulls no new dependency, CI-enforced | `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:86-89` asserts `jira` is NOT importable in the clean-core wheel, alongside langchain/langgraph/anthropic/inspect_ai/opentelemetry |
| 9 | no location-pinned module moved; `_loader.py` untouched | `adf.py`, `outbound_fields.py`, `comment_limits.py` all still under `adapters/jira/`. Their ONLY relocation (`f72a8d7c3f`, ticket dfb9) belongs to epic **bbf1** and landed **2026-07-22**, two weeks before e369's first child commit (2026-08-04). `git log --since=2026-08-03 -- _loader.py` is **empty** |
| 10 | exactly one status map, one priority map in `adapters/` | `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` dict literal defined once (`jira_family/value_maps.py:78`); `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA` once (`:22`). Other occurrences are imports/references, not definitions |
| 11 | non-`https` rejected unless `allow_insecure`; TLS never disabled | `jira_datacenter/settings.py:18` — "TLS/scheme validator (non-`https` rejected unless `allow_insecure=true`)"; `retry.py:149` records that `allow_insecure` "governs the URL scheme only" and does not affect certificate verification |
| 12 | operator docs: least-privilege scope + CA bundle | `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:30` (service account, not a person); `docs/user-guide.md:405` documents `ca_bundle` for internal-CA/self-signed and states certificate verification is **never** disabled, "disabling it would make the `https` requirement theatre" |
| 13 | `reconciler.resolved_statuses` validated config key | `src/rebar/_config_schema.py:462` — `resolved_statuses: list[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"])` |
| 14 | live DC harness GREEN end to end | harness run **30986591446** at `0df44dcbc9` on `main`: **62 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 ERRORED**, canary `collected=63 executed=62 skipped=1` — nothing silently skipped. Verified from the job log, not the run's green tick |

### One correction found during this pass

My first check reported `comment_limits.py` MISSING and I nearly recorded an AC9 violation. **That was my
wrong path guess** (`rebar_reconciler/comment_limits.py`), not a moved module — it lives at
`adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`. Located it before concluding, per the rule that an absence is not
evidence until the scan itself is checked. That rule caught seven false conclusions in this session
and this was the eighth.

### Why this is a force-close and what it does NOT claim

The completion verifier **cannot produce a verdict for this epic** — four exhaustions, and
[rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e] proved the cause is not capacity: three of four instrumented runs LOOPED
(one repeated an identical call 144x), and the clean run exhausts on genuine breadth against a flat
240-request budget. A resource exhaustion is **not a verdict**, and the gate's only documented exit
from that state is this force.

So this close records: **operator authorization plus a manual, evidenced verification of all 14
criteria** — NOT a passing completion verification. The distinction is deliberate and the audit trail
says so. Everything the epic delivered is landed, reviewed through two independent Gerrit gates, and
certified at the child level; only the epic's own machine verdict is absent, and the reason is a
defect in the verifier, tracked at [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e], [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0],
[rebar:895c-3eb2-043a-4de1] and [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86].
